2026FIFA北中米ワールドカップの公式テーマソング「Dai Dai」が、米ビルボードのメインシングルチャート「ホット100」の歴史を完全に塗り替えたことは記憶に新しいです。
1990年のイタリア大会からFIFA公式テーマソング制度が正式に導入されて以来、世界各国のトップアーティストたちが歌い上げてきた数多くのワールドカップソングの中で、米ビルボード「ホット100」にチャートインし、大衆的なメガヒットを証明した楽曲は歴史上わずか4曲に過ぎません。
シャキーラとバーナ・ボーイの「Dai Dai」が17位に輝き首位に君臨したことに続き、2位は2010年南アフリカ大会の際にシャキーラが歌い世界中で愛された「Waka Waka」（最高位38位）が占めています。それに続き、1998年フランス大会のリッキー・マーティンによる「The Cup of Life」（最高位45位）、2014年ブラジル大会のピットブル、ジェニファー・ロペス、クラウディア・レイチによる「We Are One」（最高位59位）が名を連ねています。 
この結果、シャキーラはビルボード・ホット100の「トップ40」の壁を突破したワールドカップ公式テーマソングを2曲（「Waka Waka」「Dai Dai」）も保有する、地球上で唯一無二のアーティストとなりました。
彼女が手にした「ワールドカップ史上最高の歌姫」という栄冠の裏には、彼女ならではの温かい社会貢献と善良な影響力があり、その感動をさらに深めています。
本公式テーマソング「Dai Dai」から得られる個人音源ロイヤリティ著作権収益の100%をFIFAとグローバル・シチズン（Global Citizen）が主催する「FIFAグローバル・シチズン教育基金」に全額寄付することを発表、さらに全世界で累計観客数330万人を突破し、ヒスパニック系アーティストのツアーとして史上最高の興行成績1位を記録しているワールドツアー「Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran」のチケット売上からもチケット1枚につき1ドルずつを同基金にマッチング寄付✰

Hi. I don’t know who will ever read this. Maybe these words will disappear among thousands of others and never be noticed. But if, somehow, this message found its way to you, maybe there’s something here that your heart needed to hear today.

I don’t know what you’re going through.

I don’t know how many nights you’ve spent wondering if you were ever good enough, or how many times you’ve looked around and felt as though everyone else was moving forward while you were standing still.

But please remember this:

What you’re going through right now does not have to define the rest of your story.

Maybe you feel like you’re not enough. Maybe your dreams seem impossibly far away. Maybe you’ve made mistakes, missed opportunities, or simply grown tired of trying without seeing anything change.

But tomorrow still exists.

And as long as another morning comes, there is another chance to learn, to change, to rebuild, and to begin again.

You don’t need to have your entire life figured out today. You don’t have to fight every battle at once. Sometimes, being strong simply means making it through one more day.

Please, don’t let one painful chapter become the definition of your entire life.

You are more than a bad grade.
More than a failure.
More than a rejection.
More than your mistakes.
And so much more than the things people have said about you.

There is something within you that you may not have even discovered yet.

There are places you haven’t seen.
People you haven’t met.
Dreams you haven’t lived.
Memories you haven’t made.
And versions of yourself you haven’t had the chance to become.

Maybe everything feels cloudy right now.

But no night lasts forever.

So keep going.

Walk slowly if you need to. Rest when you need to. Begin again as many times as it takes. And when everything becomes too heavy to carry alone, please reach out to someone. You were never meant to carry every burden in silence.

And if you can’t believe in yourself today, then let these words hold a little hope for you until you can:

I believe in you.

I believe there are still beautiful pages waiting to be written in your story.

And above all, remember this:

Jesus believes in you.

He knows every tear you’ve cried, every fear you’ve carried, and every silent thought you’ve kept hidden in your heart. Even when you feel lost, forgotten, or alone, you are still loved.

So please, don’t believe that this is the end.

Maybe it’s only a difficult chapter.

There is still hope.

There is still a road ahead.

There is still tomorrow. ❤️

A música "Dai Dai", de Shakira e Burna Boy, é um hino motivacional com forte temática esportiva e de superação. A letra incentiva o ouvinte a persistir em seus objetivos, destacando que as dificuldades do passado servem como base para construir a força necessária para o sucesso (0:20 - 0:35).

Pontos principais da canção:

Superação: A música enfatiza que, apesar dos "altos e baixos" e da "dor", é necessário continuar em frente para alcançar os sonhos (1:09 - 1:23).
Referência ao esporte: A letra cita diversos nomes icônicos do futebol mundial, como Pelé, Maradona, Messi e Mbappé, além de várias nações, reforçando o espírito de competição e glória (2:58 - 3:08).
Mensagem de união e força: O refrão transmite uma energia contagiante, focada na determinação individual e na capacidade de transformar o esforço pessoal em conquistas, descritas metaforicamente como "transformar lágrimas em ouro" (2:04 - 2:15).

Here is an emotional essay in English about a World Cup song (such as "Waka Waka" or "Hayya Hayya") written with the same raw, reflective, and personal tone:
To be completely honest, whenever I press play on a iconic World Cup anthem, I am immediately pulled into a wave of pure nostalgia without any warning. It is never just a simple track to get people hyped for a tournament; the moment those pulsing rhythms and energetic vocals fill the room, everything else around me seems to fade into the background. It forces me to pause whatever I am doing and fully immerse myself in the memories that the music brings back.
What hits me the hardest about a World Cup song is not just the catchy beat, but the overwhelming sense of unity and shared passion it creates. It taps right into a core emotion that so many of us feel but rarely put into words: the magic of a global moment. Listening to the lyrics, I am instantly transported back to those late summer nights—sitting in front of the TV with family and friends, holding our breath with every attack, and screaming at the top of our lungs when a goal was scored. The anthem carries the weight of millions of voices cheering together across continents, blurring boundaries and bringing complete strangers under one rhythm.
Yet, beyond the excitement and celebration, the song also leaves me with a quiet, bittersweet feeling. A World Cup only comes around once every four years, making each anthem a marker of a specific chapter in our lives. Hearing it again feels like opening a time capsule. It makes me reflect on who I was during that tournament, who was sitting beside me, and how much things have changed since then. Some friends from those viewing parties have drifted away, and time has moved on, but the song preserves those exact moments of pure, unadulterated joy intact.
When the final beat fades away, a quiet stillness remains. The song gives me a much-needed moment to slow down, smile at the past, and appreciate how deeply sports and music can bind our memories together. It serves as a beautiful reminder that while tournaments end and years pass, the emotions, the unity, and the golden memories of youth stay with us forever.

🐦 At first glance, this little shorebird doesn't look like a record-breaker. But its journey stunned scientists.

In 2022, a young bar-tailed godwit known by the identification tag "B6" completed one of the most extraordinary migrations ever recorded. The bird flew from Alaska to Tasmania, Australia—a journey of approximately 13,560 kilometers (8,425 miles)—without landing once.

The nonstop flight lasted 11 days, crossing the vast Pacific Ocean and setting the record for the longest nonstop flight ever documented by a bird.

How is that even possible?

Before migration, bar-tailed godwits undergo an incredible transformation. They nearly double their body weight by storing large amounts of fat, which serves as fuel for the entire journey. During flight, they conserve energy by taking advantage of favorable winds and even reduce the size of some internal organs that aren't needed until they reach their destination.

Scientists tracked B6's remarkable voyage using a lightweight satellite transmitter, allowing them to follow the bird's route from start to finish. Even more astonishing, this was B6's first southbound migration, proving that these birds are capable of navigating thousands of miles with extraordinary precision from a very young age.

The story of the bar-tailed godwit is a reminder that some of the world's greatest endurance athletes aren't the largest or the fastest—they're often the smallest, quietly accomplishing feats that seem almost impossible.

From the group stage onwards, they showed confidence, discipline, and excellent teamwork. Their players controlled possession, created numerous scoring opportunities, and defended effectively when under pressure. Rather than relying on individual moments of brilliance alone, Spain’s success came from every player understanding their role and working together as a unit. This collective approach allowed them to overcome strong opponents and remain unbeaten on their path to lifting the trophy.

Another major reason for Spain’s victory was the quality of their attacking football. They combined quick passing, intelligent movement, and clinical finishing to break down even the strongest defences. Their forwards and midfielders constantly created chances, while full-backs contributed to attacks by providing width and accurate crosses. Spain’s ability to dominate possession meant that opponents often struggled to regain the ball, giving Spain control over the pace and rhythm of matches. This attacking style not only entertained supporters but also produced the goals needed to progress through each knockout round.

Spain’s defensive organisation was equally important in securing the World Cup title. The defenders remained calm under pressure, communicated effectively, and limited opponents’ scoring opportunities. The goalkeeper made several crucial saves at key moments, giving the team confidence and stability from the back. Throughout the tournament, Spain demonstrated excellent positioning, disciplined pressing, and the ability to recover possession quickly after losing the ball. Their defensive strength ensured that even when matches were closely contested, they remained difficult to break down.

The team’s mentality also played a significant role in their success. Winning a World Cup requires resilience, determination, and the ability to perform under immense pressure. Spain showed these qualities in every stage of the competition, remaining focused even in difficult matches. The players displayed confidence without becoming complacent, while the coaching staff made effective tactical adjustments whenever needed. Strong leadership both on and off the pitch helped the squad stay united, motivated, and committed to achieving their ultimate goal.

Finally, Spain deserved to win the World Cup because they combined technical excellence, tactical intelligence, physical fitness, and teamwork better than any other team in the tournament. They consistently adapted to different opponents while maintaining their own style of play. Every victory reflected careful preparation, hard work, and outstanding performances from the entire squad rather than just a few individuals. By defeating some of the world’s strongest national teams and maintaining a high standard throughout the competition, Spain proved they were worthy World Cup champions and earned their place in football history.

O vídeo oficial da música "Dai Dai", de Shakira e Burna Boy, é uma celebração vibrante do futebol e da união global. Com uma estética visualmente rica, o vídeo intercala cenas de diversos jogadores de futebol famosos (0:00-0:07, 3:00-3:07), crianças brincando em um campo de terra com uma árvore imponente (0:08, 0:40, 2:09), e Shakira performando coreografias em cenários distintos, como aos pés do monumento Anjo da Independência na Cidade do México (0:11, 0:20, 1:15) e uma representação cósmica da Terra (1:17, 1:42, 3:13).

Pontos principais do vídeo:

Participação de Estrelas: O vídeo presta homenagem a ícones do esporte, citando nomes como Pelé, Maradona, Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo e Mbappé (2:52-3:06), ressaltando o legado e a paixão pelo futebol.
Temática de Superação: A letra da música foca em força, resiliência e a capacidade de transformar dificuldades em conquistas ("What broke you once made you strong" - 0:31, 3:30).
Energia Contagiante: O clímax do vídeo acontece com uma coreografia em grupo no gramado de um estádio, reunindo bailarinas e os artistas, culminando em uma comemoração com fogos de artifício (3:35-3:57).

A música carrega uma mensagem inspiradora sobre seguir desejos, escrever a própria história e acreditar no próprio valor, tudo embalado pelo ritmo e pela energia contagiante que marca as colaborações para eventos globais de futebol.

Ikou (Japanese for "let's go")
Dale (Spanish for "go ahead")
Allez (French for "go")
Let's go (English)

Dai Dai is not just a song; it is a silent 'thank you' from a man in a corner of the world who is trying to heal through your unique voice. Honestly, this song is so bland and doesn't move me at all, unlike Shakira's "Waka Waka" from the 2010 World Cup. That song was completely different and much more beautiful; it touched our hearts and stirred deep emotions. Even her anthem for the 2014 World Cup is far superior. This video looks like a copy of the 2010 video, with African children dancing, even though the tournament isn't in Africa! Back in 2010, the presence of Africans in the video was perfectly understandable because their country and continent were hosting the tournament, and it was a way to showcase their culture. Now, the tournament is being held in the US, Canada, and Mexico, so what do African children have to do with it? I certainly don't mean to be offensive or racist, but the point is that it doesn't make sense, and the song as a whole is bland, just like the 2026 World Cup, unfortunately. 
 
In short: Shakira's anthems from previous World Cups were far superior.

I believe Shakira is using the image of African kids playing and enjoying her company to connect with viewers — especially those who loved "Waka Waka."
I have two opinions:
The generous view — She's just enjoying the music, and showing African kids reminds the world they exist.
The critical view — This is really messed up, because she's using African kids as props for nostalgia or emotional effect.

1. Indignación nacional y rechazo del pueblo

​El Ángel no es un adorno urbano; es el corazón de la memoria histórica de México y el lugar donde descansan quienes dieron su vida por la patria. Ver a una artista internacional montada sobre los hombros de la Victoria Alada o usando el mausoleo como pista de baile —ya sea de forma real o mediante edición digital— desataría una ola de indignación inmediata.

​El pueblo mexicano, que trabaja diariamente y defiende con orgullo su soberanía, sentiría esto como un insulto directo a su dignidad.

​Las redes sociales y los medios de comunicación exigirían un boicot inmediato, acusando a la producción de una frivolidad imperdonable y de pisotear un símbolo sagrado para la nación.

​2. Violación a la Ley de Símbolos Patrios y Monumentos

​En México, el Monumento a la Independencia está estrictamente protegido por la ley a través del Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia (INAH) y la Ley Federal sobre Monumentos y Zonas Arqueológicos, Artísticos e Históricos.

​Prohibición absoluta: Jamás se otorgan permisos para filmaciones comerciales, videoclips musicales o espectáculos que demeriten la solemnidad del monumento.

​Si se usó pantalla verde: Aunque físicamente no se haya tocado la estructura, el uso de la imagen de un monumento histórico nacional con fines de lucro y entretenimiento de este tipo genera severas sanciones legales, demandas por parte del Gobierno Federal y la exigencia inmediata de retirar el video de todas las plataformas globales.

​3. Consecuencias políticas y diplomáticas

​El Gobierno de México, a través de la Secretaría de Cultura y la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, emitiría un pronunciamiento enérgico de rechazo. Al tratarse de un monumento que representa la soberanía del país ante el mundo, el acto se catalogaría como una ofensa de Estado. Los funcionarios que hubieran permitido cualquier tipo de acercamiento o escaneo del monumento se enfrentarían a destituciones y juicios penales.

​4. Un golpe devastador a su carrera en México

​México es el mercado musical más importante para cualquier artista de habla hispana. Cruzar la línea del respeto a la Independencia y a los héroes nacionales significaría un quiebre definitivo con el público mexicano. El rechazo no sería solo de las autoridades, sino de los millones de ciudadanos que diariamente construyen el país y que exigen que la memoria de su historia se trate con el máximo respeto y Solemnidad.

​Los símbolos de la libertad de los pueblos no son herramientas de mercadotecnia; son altares cívicos que se respetan sin excepción.

Shakira,
(This comment is for your next World Cup song 2030)

I have been one of your fans since my childhood. "Waka Waka" and "La La La" were phenomenal songs and music videos. "Dai Dai" is also a great song, and your performance is undoubtedly at its peak.

However, I don't think "Dai Dai" will have the same impact as "Waka Waka." In my opinion, the music video feels more like a Shakira music video than a World Cup-dedicated video. The focus seems to be around 80% on Shakira and 20% on football.

One of the reasons "Waka Waka" became such a massive hit was not only because of the music, but also because football fans could truly feel the spirit of the game through the video. The celebrations, emotions, iconic moments, and passion of football (which was shown in the video) created a deep connection between the song and the sport.

For a World Cup theme song, I believe it's important to connect people with the game, not just with the singer. "La La La" also felt more football-centered and engaging than "Dai Dai."

This is just my personal opinion as a longtime fan who genuinely loves your music and appreciates the energy and passion you bring to every performance.

In case someone who wants to know.

"Dai Dai" is an Italian slang exclamation that roughly means "come on!" or "let's go!". In her 2026 FIFA World Cup song with Burna Boy, Shakira uses the phrase to motivate, hype up fans, and encourage players to "give it their all" on the pitch.

The anthem features similar motivational phrases translated into multiple languages throughout the chorus, including:

Ikou (Japanese for "let's go")
Dale (Spanish for "go ahead")
Allez (French for "go")
Let's go (English)

Overcoming Adversity: The lyrics emphasize that challenges make one stronger and that believing in oneself is the key to achieving one's dreams and reaching the "top of your game" (1:09-1:23, 2:19-2:34).
Sports Celebration: The song pays homage to legendary athletes from various sports and countries, including Pelé, Maradona, Messi, Mbappé, and Cristiano Ronaldo, highlighting the global nature of sports and the unity it brings (2:58-3:09).
Energetic Vibe: The track, featuring the catchy refrain "Dai dai iko," serves as a motivational "let's go" call, encouraging listeners to follow their desires and "bring it like you mean it" (0:52-1:08, 1:26-1:32).

Esta sí me parece una canción digna de un Mundial: alegre, enérgica y capaz de conectar con millones de aficionados sin importar su país o su forma de pensar. El fútbol debería ser una celebración que una a las personas alrededor de una misma pasión.
Por eso no comparto la elección de la canción que interpretará Julieta Venegas. Considero que una Copa del Mundo merece una propuesta musical que represente el entusiasmo, la emoción y el espíritu universal del deporte, y no una que pueda percibirse como divisiva o alejada de lo que muchos aficionados esperan de este evento.
Y lo digo siendo mexicano. Mi crítica no tiene que ver con nacionalidades ni con la trayectoria de los artistas, sino con la convicción de que el Mundial debe estar acompañado por canciones que inspiren unidad, alegría y orgullo futbolero para todos.

I’m disappointed with this song. I was genuinely looking forward to a real global celebration, especially with the inclusion of an African artist and the strong visuals, which are well done.

But naming select countries makes no sense for a World Cup anthem. If you’re going to name countries in a song meant to represent the world, then name ALL participating nations. Otherwise, don’t name any at all.

Selective representation defeats the entire purpose of calling it a global anthem. With a 4-minute track, there was more than enough time to do it properly. Instead, it turns into a partial shoutout list.

Especially since these songs are meant to commemorate real history and real-time global moments, this kind of selective naming feels inconsistent with the purpose of the record.

At that point, it should’ve simply been titled FIFA 2026 Anthem—not a curated list of countries.

It’s also inconsistent how “let’s go” is said in multiple languages tied to participating nations, yet not all countries are named in the song itself. If it’s truly meant to represent the World Cup, the representation should match the message.

Football, especially the World Cup, is a global celebration of noble values: fair competition, solidarity, collective joy, and pure human effort. It has absolutely nothing to do with a woman's naked or semi-naked body, nor with sexual innuendo.
When we see almost-nude dancers gyrating in an official World Cup song, we must ask seriously: What logical connection is there between provocative hip movements and a player scoring a goal? The answer: none whatsoever. This link is entirely artificial, and its sole purpose is to grab attention through a cheap, overused tool: the commodification of the body. 

Some defend this under the guise of "freedom of expression" or "empowerment." But freedom of expression is not absolute when the work reaches hundreds of millions of people of all ages and cultures, including children. Displaying the body sexually at a family sports event is not freedom; it is imposing a vulgar consumerist culture onto a pure event. True female empowerment does not come from imitating tools of titillation crafted by the male gaze, but by showcasing women's talents, minds, and humanity – not their private parts. 

The song was an opportunity to celebrate the beauty of sports and unite people. Instead, it turned into a cheap catalog for visual arousal. It is sad that the entertainment industry still believes a woman's body is the "secret ingredient" to guarantee commercial success, even when the subject is totally unrelated. This is an insult to sports, an insult to art, and an insult to the audience's intelligence. 

There is no organic link between football and the naked body. The use of nudity here is blatant commercial exploitation, masking intellectual and artistic emptiness. Sports are better than this. The audience is smarter than this. And women deserve more than being a provocative poster for the World Cup.

Considero que, si se hubiera trabajado más la letra, habría conectado mejor con el espíritu y la emoción de un Mundial. No todo se trata de bailar; también importa que la letra transmita pasión, unión y la verdadera fiebre mundialista. 

Si a alguien no le gusta esta opinión, está bien. Cada quien tiene sus gustos y puntos de vista diferentes.

Back when I was in elementary school, I had a crush on a girl in my class named Manar.

Manar was incredibly beautiful. Almost every boy in school wanted to talk to her. I was never the type to follow the crowd, so I never tried to be one of them.

About a week before our monthly math exam, Manar switched seats with another classmate, and suddenly she was sitting right next to me.

I was unbelievably happy, but I had no idea how to show it.

After recess, I came back to class carrying a Cola Jelly for her. I gave it to her before the lesson started.

She smiled and said,

"Wow! I love these. How did you know?"

I smiled, fixed my shirt, and replied,

"I just knew." 😃

On the day of the exam, I noticed she was unusually quiet. I figured she was nervous.

I had studied really hard. Besides that, my mother always told me:

"Never let anyone copy from you. First, because it's wrong. Second, because nobody should benefit from your hard work without earning it."

Halfway through the exam, I had almost finished.

I looked over at Manar and saw tears in her eyes.

Suddenly, every word my mother had ever said about cheating disappeared from my mind.

Without thinking, I switched papers with her in less than a second, while a voice inside my head seemed to tell her:

"Don't worry."

She stopped crying and gave me a smile I'll never forget.

When she handed my paper back, I was so distracted that I submitted it without writing some of the required symbols at the end of my answers.

A couple of days later, we got our results.

Manar came first in the class with a perfect score: 50/50.

I came second with 48/50.

Honestly, I wasn't upset.

I knew I had solved everything correctly and only lost marks because I ran out of time.

More importantly, I was genuinely happy for Manar.

I felt like I had shared her success and contributed to her happiness.

I even decided to buy her two Cola Jellies this time.

After recess, I went to congratulate her and give her the treats.

But when I entered the classroom, the seats had been rearranged again.

Manar was sitting far away.

Every time I looked at her, she avoided eye contact.

I tried talking to her after school, but she rushed away without saying a word.

That evening, my mother gave me a serious lecture about the two marks I had lost.

I accepted the scolding because it was still much better than having her discover the real reason.

I went to my room and cried.

It was probably the first time in my life that I cried that hard.

Apparently, my father noticed.

The next Friday, after prayer, we were walking home when he asked:

"What's wrong with you? Why were you crying the other day?"

I told him the whole story.

He laughed so hard and said:

"That girl played you, you little fool! All this because she smiled at you? Imagine what would've happened if she had actually said something nice!" 😂

Then he said:

"Listen carefully. Do exactly what I'm about to tell you.

Act normal. Be kind. Treat her well.

But when the next exam comes, focus on your own paper and nothing else.

Even if she's giving birth right next to you." 😂

And that's exactly what I did.

The next exam arrived.

Manar started crying again.

Every time I felt sorry for her, I remembered what had happened before, and I remembered my father's advice.

The next day, we received our results.

I scored 50/50 and came first in the class.

Manar scored 21/50 and failed.

The whole class was shocked.

"Miss, how did Manar fail?"

The teacher laughed and said:

"Well, it seems the miracle that happened last time decided to take the day off." 😎

And she looked at me over her glasses.

I went home feeling proud of myself.

But deep inside, I still felt a little guilty.

So I asked my father:

"Dad, was I mean? Did I make her fail?"

He smiled and replied:

"No.

You weren't cruel.

You had simply given her more importance than she deserved.

Now you've put her back in her proper place."

And ever since that day, I stopped putting people on a pedestal and giving them more value than they deserve...

And for some reason, I never ate Cola Jelly again. ❤️

— Nader Al-Shafey

The chants are here, the passion is here, it's dynamic, it's something that makes you run and shoot in a ball. It's unsophisticated af, but football and fans have never been sophisticated, it's never been the goal. It's pure energy.

Have you ever played football? Have you ever seen English/French/German pubs during a championship? Football comes from England, Europe. A continent where most of history has been about war, about chants, about fighting for glory, for power, for the people, to unite everyone. And it's still here today in sports competitions, especially football.

I think it’s too early to compare “Dai Dai” with “Waka Waka.”
World Cup songs grow through memories, emotions, and the experiences people live during the tournament. 
“Dai Dai” has only been out for a week, so it hasn’t had the time yet to create that emotional connection with people.
It would be like asking people one week after “Waka Waka” was released which World Cup song was better? Back then, people still didn’t have all the iconic moments, celebrations, and memories connected to it.

To really compare them, we should at least wait until the World Cup is over, because that’s when these songs truly become part of people’s lives and emotions.
Honestly, I think “Dai Dai” has huge potential to become just as memorable as “Waka Waka” — but we need to give it time first.

In case someone who wants to know.

"Dai Dai" is an Italian slang exclamation that roughly means "come on!" or "let's go!". In her 2026 FIFA World Cup song with Burna Boy, Shakira uses the phrase to motivate, hype up fans, and encourage players to "give it their all" on the pitch.

The anthem features similar motivational phrases translated into multiple languages throughout the chorus, including:

Ikou (Japanese for "let's go")
Dale (Spanish for "go ahead")
Allez (French for "go")
Let's go (English)

Don't get me wrong, I'm not MAGA or anything. But WC2026 is in US and Mexico. So why it's songs video takes place in Africa and Brasil?

The video is part of a movement called We Are Ready, the same one that players mention at the beginning. It consists of raising 100 million dollars and 100 percent of the proceeds from the song and the video goes to education works for children in extreme poverty in the world.

It is an effort of a new foundation of Global Citizan and FIFA, being Shakira part of the advisory board of the foundation they created.
In the video, Shakira sings from the places where these children are, in Africa, in the Favelas, etc.

The song talks about the greats of football and their difficult path, about the tears, and about the dirt and sweat that turn to gold. The video shows you how one of those greats that the song talks about can be one of those kids if they have access to education, and how we can change their luck if they have opportunities. That is why it shows the poorest places and ends up in a stadium. From the poorest places to the stadium. The Power of Education.

En 2010 me encantaba, y todavía lo hace, Waka Waka como cancion del mundial porque tenía sentido y propósito dentro de su contexto (una canción con ritmo y letras africanas para un mundial en SUDAFRICA) pero esta cancion es un sinsentido total. El nombre, Dai Dai, es italiano. Italia tristemente no va a competir en el mundial. La escena con los niños al comienzo tiene detrás un baobab, un arbol que es típico de Madagascar. El ritmo, musicaldad y los "temas" del video/canción nada tienen que ver con los paises sedes (MEXICO, ESTADOS UNIDOS y CANADA). Además de que se perdieron la oportunidad de que cada uno de los jugadores al comienzo dijera el "we are ready" en su idioma nacional, apesar de que Messi haya dicho algo en ingles. En fin, como cancion muy bien, como cancion para un mundial, EN MI OPINION, deja mucho que desear y esta muy lejos de lo que llegó a ser y es Waka Waka.


In 2010 I loved, and still does, Waka Waka as a World Cup song because it had meaning and purpose within its context (a song with African rhythm and lyrics for a World Cup in SOUTH AFRICA) but this song is total nonsense. The name, Dai Dai, is Italian. Italy is sadly not going to compete in the World Cup. The scene with the children at the beginning has a baobab tree behind it, a tree that is typical of Madagascar. The rhythm, musicality and the "themes" of the video/song have nothing to do with the host countries (MEXICO, UNITED STATES and CANADA). In addition to the fact that they missed the opportunity for each of the players at the beginning to say "we are ready" in their national language, despite the fact that Messi has said something in English. In short, as a very good song, as a song for a World Cup, IN MY OPINION, it leaves a lot to be desired and is very far from what Waka Waka became and is.

For all the people who do not understand why Africa or do not understand the video in general.

The video is part of a movement called We Are Ready, the same one that players mention at the beginning. It consists of raising 100 million dollars and 100 percent of the proceeds from the song and the video goes to education works for children in extreme poverty in the world.

It is an effort of a new foundation of Global Citizan and FIFA, being Shakira part of the advisory board of the foundation they created.
In the video, Shakira sings from the places where these children are, in Africa, in the Favelas, etc.

The song talks about the greats of football and their difficult path, about the tears, and about the dirt and sweat that turn to gold. The video shows you how one of those greats that the song talks about can be one of those kids if they have access to education, and how we can change their luck if they have opportunities. That is why it shows the poorest places and ends up in a stadium. From the poorest places to the stadium. The Power of Education.

The video is part of a movement called We Are Ready, the same one that players mention at the beginning. It consists of raising 100 million dollars and 100 percent of the proceeds from the song and the video goes to education works for children in extreme poverty in the world.

It is an effort of a new foundation of Global Citizan and FIFA, being Shakira part of the advisory board of the foundation they created.
In the video, Shakira sings from the places where these children are, in Africa, in the Favelas, etc.

The song talks about the greats of football and their difficult path, about the tears, and about the dirt and sweat that turn to gold. The video shows you how one of those greats that the song talks about can be one of those kids if they have access to education, and how we can change their luck if they have opportunities. That is why it shows the poorest places and ends up in a stadium. From the poorest places to the stadium. The Power of Education.

The contemporary pop music landscape is increasingly dominated by transnational collaborations aimed at merging different geographical and cultural markets. In this context, "Dai Dai", featuring Colombian global icon Shakira and Nigerian Afrobeat heavyweight Burna Boy, stands out as a musical project of remarkable interest and executive precision.

From a strictly sonic perspective, the track is built on a rhythmic foundation heavily influenced by modern Afrobeat, characterized by syncopated percussion, warm basslines, and a mid-tempo groove that encourages movement without ever becoming frantic. The production is clean, minimal yet layered, leaving ample space for the vocal performances of both artists.
Shakira navigates these frequencies with ease, utilizing her signature timbre and vocal inflections to connect English verses with catchy, rhythmic choruses. Burna Boy’s entrance provides the track with a deeper, more textured quality; his warm vocals, deeply rooted in African sounds, perfectly counterbalance the pop brightness of the Barranquilla-born singer. The contrast between the two voices works effectively, creating a fluid and seamless listening dynamic.

The music video adopts a high-budget visual aesthetic that celebrates the intersection of sports, dance, and multiculturalism, with an undeniable focus on the world of football. The opening and closing sequences, featuring cameos from global football legends and current stars (including Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappé, Ronaldinho, Cristiano Ronaldo, and historical icons like Diego Maradona), clearly suggest the track's ambition to serve as a sports anthem or a potential theme for major football media events.

Visually, the narrative unfolds across three main conceptual settings:

The ancestral/natural element: Centered around a massive Baobab tree, where Shakira performs choreography blending belly dancing with tribal movements, accompanied by a dance troupe and a children's choir.

The urban element: Set on a rooftop within a working-class neighborhood (reminiscent of a favela or a densely populated urban area), where the color and energy of collective dancing emphasize the concepts of community and resilience.

The cosmic/iconic element: Where Shakira is depicted standing atop the planet Earth or balancing on iconic landmarks (such as the Angel of Independence in Mexico City), elevating the track to a level of almost epic universality.

The lyrics and imagery converge on classic themes of motivational pop: resilience, overcoming adversity, determination, and the unification of people through music and sports.

"Dai Dai" does not seek to disrupt musical conventions or pioneer avant-garde styles; instead, it delivers a solid, accessible pop product with immense international appeal. The combination of Shakira's global expertise in crafting stadium-sized anthems and Burna Boy's rhythmic credibility results in a well-balanced track that masterfully capitalizes on current trends in global pop music

I loved her outfit in yellow… but I’m not a fan of the high ponytail style in both the African and Brazilian set ups… the kids were amazing though🎉 maybe too much AI or green screens and I think we are saturated of these elements but this is what it is… this song is more sensual than inspirational… (except for the Dai Dai part that i LOOOVE). I think they left behind a lot of the fans emotions… which is the biggest part of the World Cup… how the people need this World Cup after everything that has happened globally… I think it was the opportunity to lift up the moral… so this is a super song but is not iconic like Waka Waka or La Copa de la Vida by Ricky Martin. People are gonna hate me for this but most modern World Cup songs do not even sound like football anymore. Even some of Shakira’s newer FIFA songs just sound like generic commercial pop.

And before people get mad yes Waka Waka worked because the 2010 World Cup was literally in South Africa. The African rhythms and vibe made perfect sense for that tournament and that is part of what made the song special. But not every World Cup is in Africa so I do not understand why every newer football anthem keeps trying to copy that same formula.

A lot of the newer songs sound like glossy TikTok club music or that Doja Cat style pop with rap vibes mixed with Afrobeats or sometimes EDM production. It is catchy but where are the chants the drums and the stadium energy?

World Cup songs are supposed to sound like 80,000 fans singing together not music for a fashion show or nightclub.

That is why songs like Wavin’ Flag The Cup of Life Matador and even Live It Up felt more like actual football anthems. They had crowd energy chanting emotion and sounded massive in a stadium.

Hell Live It Up by Will Smith is practically a forgotten World Cup song and 2018 was not even my favorite World Cup but that song still had more of a football feel than a lot of these newer songs. It actually sounded made for a tournament and for fans in a stadium.

And honestly Superstar by Pitbull for Copa América 2016 had more of a World Cup vibe than a lot of actual recent World Cup songs. That song felt built for football loud energetic dramatic and made for fans to chant along to.

Ver este video de Shakira para el Mundial 2026 me generó sentimientos encontrados. Por un lado, recuerdo cuando el fútbol era la única alegría en mi pueblo, en el campo. No había nada más que una pelota y una cancha de tierra, y eso reunía a todos. El fútbol daba sentido a los barrios y a los pueblos. Era hermoso porque era de todos.

Pero después llegaron las estrellas archifamosas, y el sueño de millones de niños ya no es jugar al fútbol por amor, sino por fama y dinero. Y más grave aún: el fútbol cruzó la línea entre lo legal e ilegal. Clubes acusados de lavar dinero, la FIFA señalada como una mafia, el Mundial de Qatar con muerte y explotación... ¿Cuándo se desvirtuó todo?

Y luego veo a Shakira, cantando y exhibiendo sus carnes en cada Mundial, como si no existieran otros talentos. Ella es buena, pero ¿es la única? Parece que el cuerpo de una mujer es parte del espectáculo obligatorio.

Pero lo más duro es ver niños de África utilizados como adorno en el video, barrios pobres como escenario exótico... cuando en la realidad, la posibilidad de ver un partido es solo para privilegiados. Las entradas son impagables para la mayoría. El fútbol dejó de ser del pueblo para ser un negocio que muestra la pobreza, pero no la soluciona.

Duele verlo, porque yo sé lo que el fútbol fue. Y sé que ya no lo es

Shakira has done it again, and FIFA has allowed it once more. It's not a matter of "rhythm," but a systematic omission. There's no valid technical justification. If the word fits phonetically and the goal is "globality," excluding an entire region (Scandinavia) or even a whole continent (Europe, previously with "Bamboo") points to a conscious decision. The lyrics of "Bamboo" provide a clear precedent: by saying "Latino, African, Asian, American," the exclusion of Europe is direct and deliberate.
In "Dai Dai," repeating regions that are already represented (like Asia through the Japanese word she used; there was no need to say Korea) while ignoring Scandinavia, Korea, and Norway works perfectly well, reinforces the feeling that they're not aiming for a real world map, but one based on other interests. It's not a compositional error, but a lack of integrity in the message of unity that FIFA and the artists are trying to sell. It's a complete contradiction to promote an event "for everyone" while simultaneously erasing parts of the map.

When an anthem meant to celebrate the unity of people deliberately excludes entire regions—or ignores them even though they would fit the meter perfectly—the message of "brotherhood" feels false and exclusionary.
These kinds of lyrical choices, like "Bamboo" or "Dai Dai," end up fueling a narrative of division rather than integration. Ultimately, what should be a global celebration becomes a tool for labeling who is "relevant" and who isn't, which is the antithesis of the spirit of sport. If the goal is peace and unity through music, erasing millions of people from the map is a surefire way to breed resentment.

Sinceramente, estoy muy decepcionado con la elección de Shakira para esta canción del Mundial. Ella es la reina de los Mundiales, así que mis expectativas eran altas. Cuando Sudáfrica fue el anfitrión, nos dio ritmos africanos. Cuando Brasil fue el anfitrión, adoptó el simbolismo brasileño de forma hermosa. Ella sabe perfectamente cómo honrar a los países anfitriones.
​Por eso duele ver que esta vez eligió el camino fácil. Con EE. UU., México y Canadá como anfitriones, una fusión única de mariachi mexicano y música country estadounidense habría sido increíble. En lugar de eso, reciclar las tendencias de Afrobeats solo porque están de moda ignora por completo la cultura de los verdaderos países anfitriones. Honestamente, la canción en sí es buena, pero es solo un tema común; no se siente como un himno del Mundial y definitivamente no está al nivel de Shakira.😭😭

​That’s why it hurts to see her take the easy way out this time. With the USA, Mexico, and Canada hosting, a unique fusion of Mexican mariachi and American country music would have been incredible. Instead, recycling African/Afrobeats trends just because they are popular completely ignores the culture of the actual host countries. Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies 
Nature of Operations 
Google was incorporated in California in September 1998 and re-incorporated in the State of Delaware in  
August 2003. In 2015, we implemented a holding company reorganization, and as a result, Alphabet Inc.  
("Alphabet") became the successor issuer to Google. 
We generate revenues by delivering relevant, cost-effective online advertising; cloud-based solutions that  
provide enterprise customers of all sizes with infrastructure, platform services, and applications; and sales of other  
products and services, such as fees received for subscription-based products, apps and in-app purchases, and  
devices. 
Basis of Consolidation 
The consolidated financial statements of Alphabet include the accounts of Alphabet and entities consolidated  
under the variable interest and voting models. Intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated. 
Unaudited Interim Financial Information 
These unaudited interim consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally  
accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP), and in our opinion, include all adjustments of a normal  
recurring nature necessary for fair financial statement presentation. Interim results are not necessarily indicative of  
the results to be expected for the full year ending December 31, 2026. We have made estimates and assumptions  
that affect the amounts reported and disclosed in the financial statements and the accompanying notes. Actual  
results could differ materially from these estimates. 
These consolidated financial statements and other information presented in this Form 10-Q should be read in  
conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and the related notes included in our Annual Report on Form  
10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 filed with the SEC. There have been no material changes to our  
significant accounting policies from our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, except  
for as described below. 
Use of Estimates  
Preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires us to make estimates and  
assumptions that affect the amounts reported and disclosed in the financial statements and the accompanying  
notes. Actual results could differ materially from these estimates due to uncertainties. On an ongoing basis, we  
evaluate our estimates, including those related to the allowance for credit losses; contingent liabilities; fair values of  
financial instruments, intangible assets and goodwill; income taxes; inventory; and useful lives of intangible assets  
and property and equipment, among others. We base our estimates on assumptions, both historical and forward  
looking, that are believed to be reasonable, and the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the  
carrying values of assets and liabilities. 
Acquired Intangible Assets 
Intangible assets with definite lives are amortized over their estimated useful lives on a straight-line basis  
generally over periods ranging from one to 10 years, and are subsequently removed from the presentation of gross  
intangible assets and accumulated amortization once they are fully amortized. 
Assets Held for Sale 
We consider assets to be held for sale in the period when all of the criteria for a qualifying plan of sale are met.  
Upon designation as held for sale, we record the assets at the lower of their carrying value or their estimated fair  
value, reduced for the cost to sell the assets, and cease depreciation. Long-lived assets classified as held for sale  
are measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis.

People are gonna hate me for this but most modern World Cup songs do not even sound like football anymore. Even some of Shakira’s newer FIFA songs just sound like generic commercial pop.

And before people get mad yes Waka Waka worked because the 2010 World Cup was literally in South Africa. The African rhythms and vibe made perfect sense for that tournament and that is part of what made the song special. But not every World Cup is in Africa so I do not understand why every newer football anthem keeps trying to copy that same formula.

A lot of the newer songs sound like glossy TikTok club music or that Doja Cat style pop with rap vibes mixed with Afrobeats or sometimes EDM production. It is catchy but where are the chants the drums and the stadium energy?

World Cup songs are supposed to sound like 80,000 fans singing together not music for a fashion show or nightclub.

That is why songs like Wavin’ Flag The Cup of Life Matador and even Live It Up felt more like actual football anthems. They had crowd energy chanting emotion and sounded massive in a stadium.

Hell Live It Up by Will Smith is practically a forgotten World Cup song and 2018 was not even my favorite World Cup but that song still had more of a football feel than a lot of these newer songs. It actually sounded made for a tournament and for fans in a stadium.

And honestly Superstar by Pitbull for Copa América 2016 had more of a World Cup vibe than a lot of actual recent World Cup songs. That song felt built for football loud energetic dramatic and made for fans to chant along to.
